recommendations.description: Conduct a joint utilization management, program integrity, and reimbursement compliance audit of FL Medicaid prior-authorized SNF - FREE STANDING admissions for LTSS Dual Eligible and LTSS Non Dual, focused on Degenerative Nervous System Disorders with MCC and Medical Back Problems without MCC, to review diagnosis concentration, site-of-care controls, denial enforcement, auth-to-claim matching, and contractual claims processing.
evidence: FL LTSS Dual Eligible free-standing SNF added +$61.3M.
FL LTSS Non Dual free-standing SNF added +$8.1M.
Admissions increased across both LTSS SNF segments.
Prior authorization required code is Y across key SNF drivers.
Degenerative Nervous System Disorders with MCC contributed +$3.0M.
Medical Back Problems without MCC showed mixed volume and unit-cost pressure.

recommendations.description: Audit FL Medicaid AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION claims to confirm authorization denial enforcement and contractual claims processing/reprocessing, and place Tampa General Hospital in a separate provider-focused review track.
evidence: FL AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION accounts for +$55.7M state delta.
Tampa General Hospital adds +$2.4M within the same authorization issue.
Both source cards are flagged requires_validation_before_action.
peer_benchmarking: Elevance Health (internal) requires auth for physician-directed tracheostomy care supplies, subject to medical necessity and benefit limits.
Centene, Cigna, and United Health show broad bundling or no-auth policies, not Florida authorization-movement guidance.

recommendations.description: Conduct a CA Medicaid AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION auth-to-claim validation and contractual claims reprocessing audit, verify authorization denial enforcement, and defer DRG-specific UM or reimbursement changes until Degenerative Nervous System Disorders with MCC and Medical Back Problems without MCC are reviewed separately.
evidence: CA AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION shows +$18.3M delta requiring validation before action.
Degenerative Nervous System Disorders with MCC account for +$12.3M inside the issue.
Medical Back Problems without MCC add +$6.0M inside the same classification shift.
peer_benchmarking: Humana reports no code-specific authorization; claims remain subject to applicable referral and authorization requirements.
Elevance Health internal summary shows no documented pattern-specific authorization notes.

recommendations.description: Conduct an auth-to-claim and claims reprocessing validation of AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION Y/N across IN, MD, and MO for Riley's Children's Health, Vaginal Delivery with O.R. Procedures Except Sterilization and/or D&C, and Depressive Neuroses before market-level policy action.
evidence: IN, MD, MO AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION totals +$12.6M.
Riley's Children's Health contributes +$8.3M within the authorization classification issue.
MD vaginal delivery claims add +$2.6M under the same pattern.
MO depressive behavioral health claims add +$1.7M under the same pattern.
Cards are flagged auth_or_mapping_shift and requires_validation_before_action.
peer_benchmarking: CareFirst BCBS maternity doula services show No Auth with specified billing requirements.
Centene global maternity package uses CPT-based bundling with No Auth.

recommendations.description: Initiate a Tampa General Hospital FL Medicaid ABD Non Dual acute inpatient audit to confirm prior authorization, contract-rate compliance, acute level-of-care appropriateness, and manual adjudication overrides, and redirect admissions failing acute criteria to alternative management or site-of-care pathways.
evidence: Tampa General ABD Non Dual acute claims increased by $2.2M.
Paid per admit at Tampa General rose about $9.9K.
FL ABD Non Dual acute utilization added $5.9M with 422 more admissions.
Tampa General TANF Standard acute claims added $336K with 63 more admissions.
Source cards show pa_required_code equals Y.
peer_benchmarking: Molina covers inpatient and outpatient hospital settings and bundles routine services.
United Health applies to inpatient and outpatient hospital facilities and bundles routine services.

recommendations.description: Launch a joint contract, claims, and utilization management audit of Riley's Children's Health for IN Medicaid PA-required non-ER IP Med/Surg CHILDRENS admissions in TANF Standard and Family Care to confirm prior-authorization-to-claim matching, enforce authorization denials, validate reimbursement to contractual terms, and assess site-of-care opportunities.
evidence: Riley's Children's Health is the dominant pediatric provider signal in IN.
Increase reflects more admissions and higher paid per admit.
PA-required CHILDRENS admissions appear in both TANF Standard and Family Care.
Separate authorization validation pattern also identifies the same provider.
peer_benchmarking: Centene denies claims with PA, PB, and PC modifiers; never-event services are non-reimbursable.

processing_log.relevance_reason: IP NF (DNE) Trend 6: The pattern is overwhelmingly volume-led, with large increases in admissions and claims in FL free-standing SNF, making utilization management KPI review and PAV analysis the most direct parent rule match.; IP NF (DNE) Trend 8: All major drivers are prior-authorized SNF services (pa_required_code = Y), and the pattern explicitly flags auth-to-claim validation and recommends UM review, so auth denial enforcement/auth-to-claim matching is highly relevant.; IP NF (DNE) Trend 3: Specific diagnosis groups contribute meaningfully within the broader surge, especially Degenerative Nervous System Disorders with MCC and Medical Back Problems without MCC, indicating diagnosis-level concentration.; IP NF (DNE) Trend 4: The increase is tightly concentrated in one service setting—SNF free-standing—so reviewing service/site-of-care drivers is directly aligned with the observed pattern.; IP NF (DNE) Trend 10: Although the surge is mainly volume-driven, paid per admit also increased and the recommended next step includes reimbursement policy review, making reimbursement method an important secondary parent rule.
